title: Anchor Dispatch — Skill-Structure Fix for Step-Anchorable Mechanisms
summary: Specifies the Skill-Structure Layer implementation of Invariant 8's anchoring requirement: for every Tier 1 mechanism whose dispatch can be anchored to a concrete workflow step, the governing skill must name the mechanism by its `subagent_type`, place the dispatch at a mechanically-unavoidable step, use a canonical prompt skeleton with a regex-parseable `Output path:` line, and place the dispatch at a structurally privileged position (top or bottom third, not the "lost in the middle" zone) of the skill file. The primary fix adds a Susceptibility Snapshot Dispatch subsection to each of the eight phase skills at the phase-end position, writing to `.rdd/audits/susceptibility-snapshot-{cycle}-{phase}.md`; existing dispatch sites (citation, argument, research-methods auditors) are audited against the canonical skeleton and position.
workflow_point: phase-end of each of the eight RDD phase skills
mechanism: canonical dispatch-prompt skeleton with regex-parseable Output path: line, placed at a structurally privileged skill-file position

links.note: ADR-064's PostToolUse hook depends on this ADR's canonical dispatch-prompt skeleton (the `Output path:` line) to extract expected output paths; this ADR is a precondition for ADR-064's compound check.

Names ADR-066's User-Tooling Layer pattern as the third alternative substrate (alongside this ADR's Skill-Structure Layer and ADR-064's Harness Layer) for anchoring Tier 1 mechanisms under Invariant 8.

Coupled to ADR-070's housekeeping path migration: the canonical paths in this ADR's dispatch skeletons must be updated in lockstep with ADR-070's migration to avoid skill-text and hook-manifest path mismatches.
